Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City Y&/.diiq.gov.ph OPINION NO. -111- 11 2025 HECTOR REUEL D. PASCUA Mayor, Municipality of Pudtol Province of Apayao Cordillera Administrative Region Pudtol Multi-Purpose Bldg., Poblacion Pudtol 3812, Apayap lydopudtol@gmail.com Dear Mayor Pascua: 1 5 SEP 2025 This refers to your electronic mail dated May 28, 2025, requesting this Department's position on whether the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) composed of an SK Chairperson and two (2) SK members is legally deemed to have a quorum and is thereby authorized to transact official business, including the appropriation and utilization of the SK Funds. It is intimated that there are some SKs in several barangays in your municipality that are currently composed of the SK Chairperson and one or two SK members only. Due to the absence of a complete set of council members, they have been hindered from fully performing their mandate, especially in the appropriation and utilization of their respective SK Funds. Hence, the subject query. At the outset, it bears noting that under Section 4231 of the Local Government Code, the default number of SK is eight (I.e., SK Chairperson and seven members). Hence, five members are required to muster a majority. Relatedly, under Section 9(b)2 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act 107423, a majority of the SK members, including the SK Chairperson, shall constitute a quorum. It is our submission that a quorum of the SK should be computed based on the number of SK officials who have been duly elected and qualified. It must be emphasized that Section 9(b) should be read in conjunction with Section 1 9(b) of the revised IRR of RA 10742, as amended by RA 11768, which provides that "SK Special Elections shall be conducted in case the number of SK officials who were elected and qualified is less than the required quorum." With the phrase "elected and qualified," it is evident therefrom that the provision on quorum in the afore-quoted Section 9(b) should mean that it does not merely pertain to the numbers, but the remaining SKs are elected and qualified. 1 "There shall be in every barangay a sangguniang kabataan to be composed of a chairman, seven (7) members, a sécretary, and a treasurer." 2 "A majority of the SK members including the SK chairperson shall constitute a quorum." 3 "Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2025" "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

In fine, our interpretation that a quorum of the SK be based on "those elected and qualified" is impelled by public policy. We hold the wordings in Section 19(b) are meant to allow the SK to functiomeven when not all of its entire membership has been elected. Accordingly, given the COMELEC postponement of the conduct of SK special elections, it is this Departments position that in a barangay where fewer SK members were duly elected and qualified, the actual number of SK members should be the baseline for determining a majority. Othenvise, requiring a minimum of five members in order to transact official business would render SKs inoperative. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA.'RPB/LLLS-LRALLD,'jam Page 2 of 2
